sections.title: A Caucus-Race and a Long Tale

sections.label: Ch. 4
sections.title: The Rabbit Sends in a Little Bill

characters.name: Alice
characters.summary: A curious, polite and rather logical young girl, bored on a riverbank.

notes.text: Follows a White Rabbit down a rabbit-hole and begins to shrink and grow.
Grows to full size at the trial, defies the Queen, and wakes on the riverbank.

characters.name: Alice’s sister
characters.summary: Reads a book without pictures or conversations on the riverbank.

characters.name: Dinah
characters.summary: Alice’s cat at home, whom she cannot stop praising to the animals.

characters.name: The White Rabbit
characters.summary: A nervous rabbit with a waistcoat and pocket-watch, always late.

notes.text: Serves as herald at the trial of the Knave.

characters.name: The Duchess
characters.summary: A great lady the White Rabbit is terrified of keeping waiting.

notes.text: Nurses a howling baby in a kitchen full of pepper and flying crockery.
Reappears oddly affectionate, finding a moral in everything.

characters.name: The Mouse
characters.summary: A touchy mouse swimming in Alice’s pool of tears.

characters.name: The Dodo
characters.summary: Organises a Caucus-race in which everybody wins.

characters.name: Bill the Lizard
characters.summary: A hapless lizard sent down the chimney of the Rabbit’s house.

notes.text: Sits on the jury at the trial.

characters.name: The Caterpillar
characters.summary: A languid, hookah-smoking caterpillar on a mushroom.

characters.name: The Pigeon
characters.summary: A pigeon convinced the long-necked Alice is a serpent.

characters.name: The Cook
characters.summary: The Duchess’s cook, who peppers everything and hurls pans.

characters.name: The Cheshire Cat
characters.summary: A grinning cat who can vanish, leaving only its grin.

characters.name: The Hatter
characters.summary: Said by the Cheshire Cat to be mad.

notes.text: Hosts a never-ending tea-party, fond of unanswerable riddles.
Is called as a nervous witness at the trial.

characters.name: The March Hare
characters.summary: Said by the Cheshire Cat to be mad too.

characters.name: The Dormouse
characters.summary: A sleepy guest wedged between the Hatter and the March Hare.

characters.name: The Queen of Hearts
characters.summary: A furious queen whose answer to everything is “Off with their heads!”

characters.name: The King of Hearts
characters.summary: The Queen’s mild husband, who quietly pardons her victims.

characters.name: The Knave of Hearts
characters.summary: Carries the King’s crown on a cushion.

notes.text: Is put on trial for stealing the Queen’s tarts.

characters.name: The card gardeners
characters.summary: Two, Five and Seven, hastily painting white roses red.

characters.name: The Gryphon
characters.summary: A gruff gryphon ordered to take Alice to the Mock Turtle.

characters.name: The Mock Turtle
characters.summary: A deeply melancholy creature with a curious education.

phases.label: Beloved pet
phases.note: Mentioning Dinah keeps frightening the creatures she meets.

phases.label: Follows him
phases.note: She chases him down the rabbit-hole.

phases.label: Mistaken for his maid
phases.note: He takes her for his housemaid, Mary Ann.

phases.label: Offends him
phases.note: She keeps talking about cats and dogs.

phases.label: Caucus-race
phases.note: He makes her hand out the prizes — and give herself her own thimble.

phases.label: Master & servant
phases.note: Bill is sent down the chimney and kicked out again.

phases.label: Gives advice
phases.note: One side of the mushroom makes her grow, the other shrink.

phases.label: A violent nursery
phases.note: The Duchess tosses her the baby, which turns into a pig.

phases.label: Unwelcome affection
phases.note: Now oddly friendly, she digs her chin into Alice’s shoulder.

phases.label: Puzzling guide
phases.note: He points her to the Hatter and the March Hare — both mad.

phases.label: Tea-party companions
phases.note: They use him as a cushion and try to put him in the teapot.

phases.label: Rude host
phases.note: “Why is a raven like a writing-desk?”

phases.label: Terrified gardeners
phases.note: She orders them beheaded for planting the wrong roses.

phases.label: On trial
phases.note: He is accused of stealing the tarts.

phases.label: “Off with her head!”
phases.note: Alice answers back at the croquet-ground.

phases.label: Defied
phases.note: Alice declares the court nothing but a pack of cards.

phases.label: Under sentence of death
phases.note: The Duchess boxed the Queen’s ears.

phases.label: Ordered beheaded
phases.note: The executioner argues you cannot behead a cat with no body.

phases.label: Guide
phases.note: The Queen orders him to take her to the Mock Turtle.

phases.label: Herald
phases.note: He reads out the accusation against the Knave.

review.notes: Spot-check chapter/scene numbers against the stated edition before marking as reviewed.
